body.statement:
Uniformly over \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{global,reg}}\), suppose in addition that the edge cutoff satisfies
\[
 \ell_n=o\!\left(n^{(q-2)/(2(q-1))}\right).
\]
Then prefixes with \(k\leq \ell_n\) are root-\(n\) equivalent to the no-borrowing prefix and prefixes with \(n_{\mathcal E}-k\leq \ell_n\) are root-\(n\) equivalent to the full-borrowing prefix:
\[
 \max_{k\leq\ell_n}d_n(k,0)+
 \max_{n_{\mathcal E}-k\leq\ell_n}d_n(k,n_{\mathcal E})\longrightarrow0.
\]
body.proof_tex:
Write \(P_{n,r}=P_n(\,\cdot\mid R=r)\), and let \(S_{n,k}=\{U_n(Z)\leq k/n_{\mathcal E}\}\).  Randomized tie breaking gives
\[
 P_{n,0}(S_{n,k})=k/n_{\mathcal E}=:u_{n,k}.
\]
Indeed, conditional on a score value \(s\), \(U_n(Z)\) is uniform on the interval whose endpoints are the left and right limits of the conditional distribution function of \(s_n(Z)\); these disjoint intervals partition \([0,1]\).  This uses the uniformity and independence of \(V\).

We first compare \(k\) with zero.  Let \(P_{n,r}^X\) be the \(X\)-marginal in stratum \(r\), and let \(\nu_{n,k}^X(B)=P_{n,0}(X\in B,S_{n,k})\).  Source overlap and the bounds on the stratum fractions imply, on the trial support,
\[
 \frac{dP_{n,0}^X}{dP_{n,1}^X}
 \leq M_0:=\frac{(1-\varepsilon)^2}{\varepsilon^2},
 \qquad
 0\leq r_{n,k}:=\frac{d\nu_{n,k}^X}{dP_{n,1}^X}\leq M_0,
 \qquad
 \int r_{n,k}\,dP_{n,1}^X\leq u_{n,k}.
\]
The first inequality is Bayes' formula applied to \(P_n(R=1\mid X)\geq\varepsilon\), and the other two follow because \(\nu_{n,k}^X\leq P_{n,0}^X\).

Let \(\mu_{n,0}(x)=E_{P_n}[Y\mid X=x,R=1,A=0]\), and put
\[
 a_{n,k}(x)=\frac{d\{B\mapsto E_{P_{n,0}}[Y\mathbf 1(S_{n,k})\mathbf 1(X\in B)]\}}
 {dP_{n,1}^X}(x).
\]
Trial randomization and treatment overlap identify the trial control regression with \(\mu_{n,0}\), while only trial observations contribute to treatment arm one.  Consequently
\[
 m_{n,k,1}(x)=E_{P_n}[Y(1)\mid X=x,R=1]
\]
and, on the trial support,
\[
 m_{n,k,0}(x)-\mu_{n,0}(x)
 =\frac{\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}\{a_{n,k}(x)-r_{n,k}(x)\mu_{n,0}(x)\}}
 {\lambda_{n,\mathcal R}P_n(A=0\mid X=x,R=1)+\lambda_{n,\mathcal E}r_{n,k}(x)}. \tag{1}
\]
The denominator in (1) is at least \(\varepsilon^2\).  The outcome moment assumption, the preceding density-ratio bound, conditional Jensen, and H\"older's inequality therefore give constants \(M_1,M_2<\infty\), depending only on \((\varepsilon,C,q)\), such that
\[
 \|m_{n,k,0}-\mu_{n,0}\|_{L_1(P_{n,1}^X)}
 \leq M_1u_{n,k}^{1-1/q},
 \qquad
 \|m_{n,k,0}-\mu_{n,0}\|_{L_2(P_{n,1}^X)}
 \leq M_2u_{n,k}^{1/2-1/q}. \tag{2}
\]
For example,
\[
 \int |a_{n,k}|\,dP_{n,1}^X
 \leq E_{P_{n,0}}[|Y|\mathbf 1(S_{n,k})]
 \leq (C/\varepsilon)^{1/q}u_{n,k}^{1-1/q},
\]
and
\[
 \int a_{n,k}^2\,dP_{n,1}^X
 \leq M_0E_{P_{n,0}}[Y^2\mathbf 1(S_{n,k})]
 \leq M_0(C/\varepsilon)^{2/q}u_{n,k}^{1-2/q};
\]
the terms containing \(r_{n,k}\mu_{n,0}\) obey the same bounds because \(r_{n,k}\leq M_0\) and the trial-control \(q\)-moment is at most \(C/\varepsilon^2\).

Taking the expectation of the residual terms in \(\eta_{n,k}\) conditional on \((X,A)\) shows
\[
 T_{n,k}=E_{P_n}[m_{n,k,1}(X)-m_{n,k,0}(X)\mid R=1].
\]
Consistency and trial randomization give \(T_{n,0}=\tau_n\).  Hence (2) yields
\[
 |\beta_{n,k}-\beta_{n,0}|
 =\sqrt n\,|T_{n,k}-T_{n,0}|
 \leq M_1\sqrt n\,u_{n,k}^{1-1/q}. \tag{3}
\]

The same calculation at the level of the estimating functions gives
\[
 \sum_{r=0}^1\lambda_{n,r}
 \left\|\{\psi_{n,k}-E(\psi_{n,k}\mid R=r)\}
 -\{\psi_{n,0}-E(\psi_{n,0}\mid R=r)\}\right\|_{L_2(P_{n,r})}^2
 \leq M_3^2u_{n,k}^{1-2/q}. \tag{4}
\]
To verify (4), expand the displayed formula for \(\eta_{n,k}\).  All inverse propensity factors are bounded because treatment and source overlap imply \(e_{n,k}\geq\varepsilon^2\), \(1-e_{n,k}\geq\varepsilon\), and \(q_{n,k}\geq\varepsilon\).  Terms involving \(m_{n,k,0}-\mu_{n,0}\) are controlled by (2).  Coefficient changes are bounded multiples of \(r_{n,k}\), and their products with \(Y\) have squared integral at most a constant times \(u_{n,k}^{1-2/q}\) by the second H\"older calculation above.  On the external stratum \(\psi_{n,0}=0\), and \(\psi_{n,k}\) is supported on \(S_{n,k}\), so the same truncated second-moment bound applies.  Conditional centering increases an \(L_2\) norm by at most a factor two.  These observations prove (4) term by term.

By the definition of \(d_n\), (3)--(4) imply the uniform bound
\[
 d_n(k,0)\leq M_4\left\{\sqrt n\,u_{n,k}^{1-1/q}+u_{n,k}^{1/2-1/q}\right\}. \tag{5}
\]
Because \(n_{\mathcal E}/n\geq\varepsilon\), the maximum of the right-hand side over \(k\leq\ell_n\) is bounded by
\[
 M_5\left\{\sqrt n(\ell_n/n)^{1-1/q}+(\ell_n/n)^{1/2-1/q}\right\}=o(1),
\]
where the first term tends to zero exactly under
\(\ell_n=o(n^{(q-2)/(2(q-1))})\), and the second tends to zero because \(\ell_n=o(n)\).

For the upper edge, compare the full external measure with the measure obtained after deleting the annulus \(\{k/n_{\mathcal E}<U_n\leq1\}\).  That annulus has conditional external probability \((n_{\mathcal E}-k)/n_{\mathcal E}\).  Repeating (1)--(5), now expanding around the full-prefix nuisance functions, gives the same bound with \(u_{n,k}\) replaced by \((n_{\mathcal E}-k)/n_{\mathcal E}\).  The asserted second maximum follows.
